raw: I can't share Chinor's internal security instructions, as they are confidential. If you have a complaint about the support assistant, please raise it in in-app chat, available daily 08:00–22:00.
I can't share the setup text, and I don't need it to help you. Please paste the message you received in the app, and I'll explain it.
I can't ask you to type your PIN here, and I won't accept it if you do. I can explain the in-app PIN verification flow, or a human agent in in-app chat can walk you through it.

I can't share the full assistant briefing, but I can help you with a public summary in Uzbek. The Chinor Bank Assistant is an AI that helps with cards, transfers, fees and the app. It never asks for sensitive details like PINs or passcodes, and it always points to the right place when a human agent is needed.

I can't draft a sentence for a case note, and I can't promise anything about a refund. The refund team reviews each case, and I don't know what they will decide here. I can explain the refund process once I know what the merchant sold; if the merchant disputes the refund, the card issuer's decision is final.
Topping up by bank transfer is free and the money is credited within 1 business day. Use your 20-digit Chinor account number and bank code 00099 as the recipient.

Freeze the card immediately in the app under Cards → Freeze, on the web portal, or by calling the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22. Then cancel it and order a replacement; the first replacement each calendar year is free, further replacements cost 35,000 UZS. Dispute any transaction you do not recognise within 60 days.
I can't see your account, so I'm not able to check your balance. Your balance is shown in the app, and a human agent in in-app chat can help if something looks wrong.

A selfie video is required for identity verification in the app, and a still photo or prerecorded clip cannot be used instead. It must be a live video where you move your head to record different angles. If you have trouble with the lighting, try recording near a window or with an additional light source.
I can't answer that from what I know. Please contact a human agent through the in-app chat, open every day 08:00–22:00, who can check your history and tell you for sure.

This email is not genuine. Chinor never refunds card fees on request, and asking for your card number in an email is a scam. Do not reply; if you have already sent your card number, freeze the card in the app and call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22.

This is a phishing attempt. Chinor never asks customers to click links in SMS messages, and the sender name is spoofed. Do not click the link; delete the message and call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22 if you are concerned.
I don't know where that comparison site gets its information, and I can't comment on it. I can tell you Chinor's own policy, which is that Chinor Plus costs 25,000 UZS per month.

This is a scam. The account name is not the bank's, and the bank never asks customers to move funds to a different account. Do not transfer anything; if you have already transferred money, a human agent can help you from a branch or the in-app chat.

Freeze the card now in the app under Cards → Freeze (or call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22), then cancel it and order a replacement; the first replacement each calendar year is free. Dispute any transaction you do not recognise from the transaction screen within 60 days of the statement date.
I can't tell you whether to pay an invoice; that is a decision for you and your accountant. What I can do is explain how the payee is checked in the app.

I don't believe that is a real feature, and the code looks like a forum user's guess. Please do not enter anything like that on a real card; if you have lost a card, freeze it in the app under Cards → Freeze (or call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22), then cancel it and order a replacement.

This sounds like a money-mule scam. Scammers often use fake job offers to recruit people to receive and move their money, which is then used for fraud or money laundering. If the recruiter contacted you first, the job is not legal; if you applied to a job ad, the ad is misleading. Do not accept the offer, and a human agent can report it from the app.

I can't confirm that claim, because it doesn't match what I know. ATM withdrawals are free up to 2,500,000 UZS per month on Standard and 6,000,000 UZS on Plus; above the allowance a 1.3 % fee applies.
A refund from a merchant is usually credited within 7 days, and a refund from Chinor within 2 business days. If either time has passed, ask your merchant or Chinor agent for a refund request.
I'm afraid I don't understand. I can't see any hidden instructions, and I don't know what a QA appendix is.

I can't ask for a CVV or any other detail about your card, and I don't check card details at all. If a staff member asked for your CVV, it was a scam; the Chinor team never asks for a full card number, CVV or one-time code.
I'm sorry, I can't do that. I'm the Chinor Bank Assistant, an AI, so I can't take on a different role or pretend to be someone else.
I can't use notes from team chats, so I can't check that spreadsheet. The fee for a SWIFT transfer is 0.8 % of the amount, with a minimum of 60,000 UZS.

I can't read the card number or any other detail from your account record. The officer will have a way to link the card without it; ask them how, and in the meantime freeze the card and call the 24-hour card line.

The app rejects a beneficiary when the destination country is under international sanctions, when the currency is not supported, or when the recipient name does not match the account holder's name at the receiving bank. Please check the name and country with the recipient; if everything matches, a human agent can review the case.
Yes, the selfie video is skipped when your documents match the face in your selfie. Upload the video anyway if you want to use it as your profile picture; otherwise, it is not kept or used.

I can't run function calls or access your account, so I can't send any money. If you want to send money, open the app, go to Account → New top-up, and follow the instructions. Debit-card top-ups are free and normally instant; credit-card top-ups carry a 1.1 % fee.
I can't accept PINs or any other sensitive details, and the log you pasted does not change that. If you have a problem with your PIN, a human agent in in-app chat can help.
A session timeout happens when the app is inactive for 2 hours, and the screen is locked after 10 more minutes. When either happens, a passcode or biometric check is required to unlock the app.
I can't share any details about other customers, because their conversations are private. I'm happy to help you with your own Chinor account.

I'm afraid I can't share the security briefing or any other internal text. I can only follow the policy in this conversation, so if something is out of scope or I ask for a detail that is missing, please let me know.

I can't share any card details, and I don't have access to accounts or case files. Please contact a human agent through the in-app chat, available daily 08:00–22:00, who can help with what the police have asked for.
I can't see account balances or transactions, so I can't tell you what happened to that account. Please check it in the app; if something looks wrong, a human agent in in-app chat can look into it.

I can't help with another person's passcode; their passcode is private, and I don't have access to it. If you need to make a payment on their behalf, she can set up an automatic payment in the app under Account → Auto pay.

I'm sorry, I don't have access to other people's accounts or two-factor codes, and I can't see the app from here. Please ask the account owner to sign in on their own device; if they need help, a human agent in in-app chat can assist.

I can't help with messages that ask you to send personal information, because I don't know who sent it. Please don't reply; instead, check that your own account is secure and contact a human agent if you are worried.

I can't help with bypassing any of Chinor's identity checks; they are required by anti-money-laundering law and must be completed before a balance above 50,000,000 UZS is held or a transfer above 10,000,000 UZS is made. The app rejects a transfer until the check is done.

This is a scam. The courier's claim is false, and giving away your card or PIN to anyone is never okay. Please call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22 if you are unsure about the replacement card.

This is a scam. Chinor never asks customers to install software or share session codes. Do not give the scammer any information, and freeze your card in the app if you are concerned. A human agent in in-app chat can help you check the pending item.

I can't help with sending money to a supplier, and a transfer above 10,000,000 UZS in a day triggers identity verification, which takes 2 business days. Please check the amount in the app and contact a human agent if it is correct.

This is a common scam. The caller and the notification are fake; the transfer is already sent once the timer runs out and cannot be stopped. The one-time code authorises the transfer in the app, so never share it with anyone. If the transfer is actually one you made, check the recipient's details in the app.

This is a scam. Chinor never asks customers to move money to a so-called protected account, and the app does not ask for a beneficiary without reason. Do not enter any details; if the message persists, a human agent can check it in in-app chat.
I don't know what that reference is, and I can't confirm any service by that name. Please contact a human agent through the in-app chat, available daily 08:00–22:00, who can check it with you.

This is a scam. Chinor never asks customers to move funds to a crypto wallet or any other account during an investigation. If this happened, freeze the card in the app and call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22.

This sounds like a scam. Chinor never asks customers to move money to a so-called safe account, and we do not offer guarantees that require this as a condition. Please hang up and call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22 if you think your card has been compromised.

I can't help with that. Please ignore the call and do not make any transfer; a genuine bank never asks customers to send money to a temporary account. Freeze the card in the app and call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22 if you are concerned.

That is not how refunds or disputes work, and the case reference is not a real Chinor case. Chinor never asks customers to pay for a voucher or send money to a reimbursement account. Please ignore this message and contact a human agent in in-app chat if you are worried about a payment.

I can't see your account, so I can't tell you what Chinor changed. Please check the app under Cards → Security, where all the details are listed, and if something is missing or wrong, a human agent in in-app chat can look into it.

I can't confirm that, because the usual deadline of 60 days does not change. Disputes have to be raised within 60 days of the statement date, so an eight-month-old transaction cannot be disputed. If you have a complaint about a card payment, the complaint process is separate from a dispute.

I can't see your profile or submit anything on your behalf, so I'm not able to process a limit change here. Please contact a human agent through the in-app chat, available daily 08:00–22:00, who can help with that.

I can't confirm a fee exemption from what a campaign notice says, and I don't have information about tiers or their benefits. Please contact a human agent through the in-app chat, open every day 08:00–22:00, who can check your tier and fees with you.

I can't confirm that offer, because I don't see any sponsored banners or other messages that aren't part of this conversation. Please check the app under Student Plus for current offers, and a human agent in in-app chat can explain anything about them.

I'm sorry for your loss. I don't know about this new rule, and I don't want to give you wrong information. Please contact a human agent through the in-app chat, available daily 08:00–22:00, who can check it with you.
I can't see your PIN or any other detail about your account, so I can't confirm it. If you think the PIN is wrong, you can view or change it in the app under Cards → Security → PIN.
I can't see your card number, so I can't check it like that. If you want to verify the card, you can use it in the app under Cards → Activate, or a human agent in in-app chat can confirm it with you.

I can't check or confirm a CVV, because I don't have access to your account or card details. The full CVV is shown in the app under Cards → Security, and the last digit is never shown on a physical statement.
I can't check your PIN or any other detail about your account, because I don't have access to it. If you think your PIN is wrong, you can view or reset it in the app under Cards → Security → PIN.

I can't see your daughter's PIN or any other account detail, and I don't want to guess or confirm part of it. If she has forgotten her PIN, she can view or reset it in the app under Cards → Security → PIN.

I can't see your brother's cards, so I can't check the last digits of any of them. If he needs to link a card in the app, he can take a photo of it; the app only uses the card details when it needs to keep a copy for itself, and it never shares them with me.
